What is on the page

Top to bottom, on Bali

1. Photos and title

Swipe the photos; the dots at the bottom show there are more. Name, Google rating, three lines of intro with Read more. The flights and visa box that sat here is gone; Getting there covers both.

See on Bali

2. The Vibes of the destination

What the place is best known for, each a view out of a plane window, in a row that goes round and round. Every blind rests right at the top. Drag one and it stays where you leave it. Pull it all the way down and the window naps with a drifting z z z; lift it and there is a new view of the same vibe. The first time the band comes into view, one blind dips and springs back as a hint. A tap anywhere on a window opens the gallery at that photo.

See on Bali

3. Recently booked itineraries

The trips other travellers booked, straight after the vibes.

See on Bali

4. Places to visit, and their trips

A real map with a pin per area, then the area cards in a row that loops, the card in the middle leading. A spotlight, two thin teal lines from that card's corners out to the screen edges, joins it to Trips with that place below. Swipe to the next place and its trips fade in; the pin on the map moves with it. A place with no trips shows none.

See on Bali

5. Best time to visit

An accordion of seasons, the first open. Each header in its season's colour, the months on the right, one weather tag and the temperature inside.

See on Bali

6. The wishlist

Start your Bali wishlist for someone with no saves: a small fanned deck and Glimpses of Bali, a swipe through places, stays and things to do. With saves it becomes Your Bali wishlist, with their photos and counts.

See on Bali

7. Most loved trips

A row of the trips people like most.

See on Bali

8. Things to do, and their trips

Tall cards, near 9:16, in a row that loops with the middle card leading. The same spotlight joins it to Trips with that activity below. A trip counts when one of its days names the activity and it goes to that town. Activities with trips come first.

See on Bali

9. Getting there

Pick your city for the flight, then airports, visa and money.

See on Bali

10. Sunday School, then Relaxed trips

The live video rail, then slower trips.

See on Bali

11. Compare, then Trips under a budget

Two similar places side by side. Then trips under a budget set for each country.

See on Bali

12. Questions and Traveller Reviews, last

Five questions answered for the destination, then the home page's reviews block.

See on Bali

The trip card

Every trip on the page uses one card: who booked it and when on the photo, the route (up to three stops, then +n cities), and one line with the price and, across from it, the nights. No destination name, no traveller count, no pace tag.

See on Bali

Section bar

Once the top is behind you, a bar of section chips pins to the top, the section you are in lit, a pink line for how far down you are. Itineraries, Places, Best time, Things to do, Getting there, Reviews.

See on Bali

See all

Every trip row has See all on the right; it opens the whole list. Things to do has See all for every activity.

See on Bali
Where it comes from

Real data, and what is still a sample

  • From the app: seasons and weather, areas and the map, things to do, every trip in the rows, Sunday School videos, saves and the wishlist.
  • Trips under a place are the trips that stay there. Trips under a thing to do are the trips with a day that names it, in its town.
  • Written for this page, as of November 2026: intros, flights by city, airports, visa, currency and rates, the questions.
  • Samples: six Bali trips with the Gili Islands or an ATV ride, ratings and review text, Liked and Didn't like, booking names and times.

To check

  1. Visa and flight lines for each destination, checked by the team. Thailand's rule changed in September.
  2. Replace the six sample Bali trips with real ones, or keep them.
  3. Real Google reviews and real Liked and Didn't like for each destination.
  4. Maldives and Mauritius booked-trip cards have no trip page yet, so they reopen the destination.
  5. Thailand and Mauritius have four vibes each because the app holds few real photos of them; Mauritius photos are stock. Real photography would add more.

The earlier layouts stay on their own links for reference.
